name: A Santiago garden

place_source.title: Wikidata: Santiago (Q2887), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A suburban garden in Santiago's Mediterranean climate: a lawn, a border of boldo and peumo, fruit trees along the fence and a Chilean wine palm, visited by thrushes, doves, parakeets and mockingbirds by day and by bats after dark.

facts.text: Santiago has a cool semi-arid climate with Mediterranean characteristics: warm, dry summers and cool, wet winters. The city centre is described as BSk with Csb patterns, and the eastern districts against the Andes as true Csb; this locale uses Csb.

source.title: Wikipedia: Santiago

facts.text: Santiago is the capital and largest city of Chile, located in the Chilean Central Valley within the Santiago Basin; Wikidata gives its coordinate location as 33.4375° S, 70.65° W and its elevation above sea level as 575 m.
The Chilean matorral, a terrestrial ecoregion of central Chile with a temperate Mediterranean climate of rainy winters and dry summers, is one of the world's five Mediterranean-climate regions.

source.title: Wikipedia: Chilean Matorral
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Chilean Matorral", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Feral monk parakeet populations are documented in Chile, and the species is unique among even nesting parrots in building large external nests in trees or manmade structures rather than using tree cavities.

source.title: Wikipedia: Monk parakeet
